judul: Annotated Datasets of Oil Palm Fruit Bunch Piles for Ripeness Grading Using Deep Learning
abstrak: The quality of palm oil is strongly influenced by the maturity level of the fruit to be processed into palm oil. Many studies have been carried out for detecting and classifying the maturity level of oil palm fruit to improve the quality with the use of computer vision. However, most of these studies use datasets in the form of images of oil palm fresh fruit bunches (FFB) with incomplete categorization according to real conditions in palm oil mills. Therefore, this study introduces a new complete dataset obtained directly from palm oil mills in the form of videos and images with different categories in accordance with the real conditions faced by the grading section of the palm oil mill. The video dataset consists of 45 videos with a single category of FFB videos and 56 videos with a collection of FFB with multiple categories for each video. Videos are collected using a smart phone with a size of 1280 × 720 pixels with .mp4 format. In addition, this dataset has also been annotated and labelled based on the maturity level of oil palm fruit with 6 categories, which are unripe, under-ripe, ripe, overripe, empty bunches and abnormal fruit.

klaim.kalimat: At the mill, Suharjito et al. graded piles of bunches from smartphone video [suharjito2023real] and released annotated datasets of piles [suharjito2023annotated].

judul: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction with point-cloud representations: From DUSt3R to VGGT and beyond
abstrak: This survey reviews feed-forward, point-cloud 3D reconstruction methods from DUSt3R to VGGT and their recent variants. Here, feed-forward primarily refers to predicting dense geometry and, when applicable, camera poses through learned network inference, without relying on classical per-scene SfM + MVS optimization as the main inference mechanism. We first formalize the reconstruction task in pose-aware and pose-free settings, and contrast feed-forward point-map regression with classical Structure-from-Motion and Multi-View Stereo pipelines. Building on this, we organize existing methods into three stages: early pairwise models typified by DUSt3R, DUSt3R-style extensions that enhance multi-view consistency, streaming, efficiency, and dynamic-scene handling, and large unified transformers such as VGGT that process tens to hundreds of views jointly, while noting differences in their inference paradigms. We analyze these models along shared axes, including scene representation, correspondence reasoning, pose regression, fusion strategies, and the role of large-scale training data. We summarize widely used 3D datasets and evaluation metrics, and provide a case study on the DTU benchmark for multi-view depth and point map estimation, highlighting accuracy-efficiency trade-offs between optimization-based and feed-forward approaches. Finally, we discuss open challenges in data scarcity, sparse-view reconstruction, non-Lambertian structures, dynamic scenes, long-context processing, and resource-efficient deployment, and outline future directions that combine feed-forward architectures with differentiable rendering, generative priors, and safety mechanisms to enable scalable and trustworthy 3D reconstruction systems.

klaim.kalimat: Reviews of tracking and re-identification outside agriculture [luo2021multiple, rakai2022data, ye2022deep] and of 3D reconstruction [saputra2019visual, zheng2026feed] provide the mechanisms but not the agricultural evidence.

judul: Fruitgaussian: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Automated Fruit Counting in Natural Orchard
abstrak: Automatic fruit counting in natural orchard environments remains challenging due to foliage occlusion, illumination variations, and inefficient 3D reconstruction methods. To address these limitations, we propose FruitGaussian, a novel 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based framework for high-fidelity orchard scene understanding and fruit counting. Our approach introduces two key innovations: a hierarchical semantic embedding mechanism that fuses multimodal features (RGB, semantics, depth) for precise fruit instance encoding, and a depth-aware regularization constraint that leverages monocular depth priors to suppress boundary artifacts and floating noise. By integrating explicit 3D Gaussian representations with differentiable rendering, FruitGaussian achieves real-time high-fidelity rendering and geometric fidelity while enabling direct point cloud extraction within seconds. Evaluations on real-world persimmon orchard datasets demonstrate a 96 % counting accuracy, surpassing Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)-based methods by 16 %. The explicit Gaussian representation enables efficient point cloud extraction within seconds, significantly advancing the practicality and robustness of vision-based yield estimation in precision agriculture.

klaim.kalimat: [hong2025fruitgaussian] | Persimmon | 3D Gaussian splatting vs NeRF-based counting | Counting accuracy 96%, reported as 16% above NeRF-based methods | Count

Implicit representations are the latest variant: FruitNeRF trains a semantic neural radiance field from posed images and clusters the extracted fruit points [meyer2024fruitnerf], FruitNeRF++ adds instance embeddings to remove fruit-specific tuning [meyer2025fruitnerf], and Gaussian splatting was reported to count persimmons with 96% accuracy, 16% above NeRF-based counting [hong2025fruitgaussian].

judul: Assigning apples to individual trees in dense orchards using 3D colour point clouds
abstrak: We propose a 3D colour point cloud processing pipeline to count apples on individual apple trees in trellis structured orchards. Fruit counting at the tree level requires separating trees, which is challenging in dense orchards. We employ point clouds acquired from the leaf-off orchard in winter period, where the branch structure is visible, to delineate tree crowns. We localise apples in point clouds acquired in harvest period. Alignment of the two point clouds enables mapping apple locations to the delineated winter cloud and assigning each apple to its bearing tree. Our apple assignment method achieves an accuracy rate higher than 95%. In addition to presenting a first proof of feasibility, we also provide suggestions for further improvement on our apple assignment pipeline.

klaim.kalimat: Assigning fruit to trees is a separate geometric problem; Zine-El-Abidine et al. solved it by aligning a harvest-time point cloud to a leaf-off winter cloud in which each tree's branches are visible (accuracy above 95%) [zineelabidine2021assigning].

judul: Mandarin count estimation with 360-degree tree video and transformer-based deep learning
abstrak: In mandarin orange production, knowing the number of mandarins on a tree is crucial for performing appropriate thinning operations. This is necessary to prevent overbearing and to maintain the size and quality of individual mandarins. However, the dense foliage of mandarin trees often obscures many fruits. Before thinning, a tree can have several hundred to several thousand mandarins, making manual counting not only labor-intensive but also exceedingly difficult. This study proposes a novel technology for automatically estimating the number of small, unripe mandarins before thinning operations using 360-degree videos of the trees. A deep neural network model leveraging Transformer architecture is designed to fuse features from various viewing angles. State-of-the-art (SOTA) unsupervised pre-training techniques, along with a custom-designed loss function, are employed to tackle the challenge of limited training data and to enhance the model's capability to capture global contextual features from images taken at multiple angles. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing methods.

klaim.kalimat: Isobe et al. fused features from different angles of a 360-degree mandarin video in a transformer and regressed the count, without an explicit identity for each fruit [isobe2025mandarin].
